title: Curiosity docket: lightweight lit notes + experiment plan
content:
Quick brain-dump after skimming three things this week + a tiny plan to validate a hypothesis about small-prefix caching impact on tail latency.

High-level question: can shallow prefix/KV caching (e.g., 32-128 tokens cached, with evictions tuned per-session) capture >80% of token reuse for our conversational workloads and cut TPU/GPU per-token compute by 20% for median requests without increasing 95p latency? If yes, we can push a conservative auto-cache suggestion in Redwood Optimize.

1) Paper: "Locality-Aware KV Caches for Long-Context Decoding" (arXiv 2026) -- quick notes
- Core idea: hierarchical cache: session-level fast cache (GPU-local), shardable segment-store (host memory), TTL-based eviction.
- Micro-result that matters: caching first 64 tokens of each user turn saved ~18% total FLOPs on web chat traces, but 95p latency moved +6ms when miss-handling used naive locking.
- My takeaway: locking/serialization on misses kills tail; need lock-free or optimistic concurrent read path for GPU-local caches.
- Open Q: how much of that is artifact of their batching strategy? they batch aggressively (up to 32) which increases miss contention.

2) Paper: "Adaptive Microbatching for Interactive Inference" (NeurIPS 2026 workshop) -- quick notes
- Proposal: per-route SLO-aware microbatcher that uses a short lookahead window (15ms) to collect requests and adapt batch size up to N based on observed latency distribution.
- Nice trick: use a cheap latency predictor (two-feature linear model) to decide when to flush early. Predictor trained on sequence length + queue time.
- Observed: 9% cost reduction while keeping p95 < target, but this depends on stable arrival patterns (bursty traffic hurts).
- Relevance: Could complement our Redwood Smart Router for hosted API; maybe used as per-tenant policy override.

3) Blog / distillation note: "Prompt-space distillation for quant-robust generation" (engineering blog, May 2026)
- Distil prompts to be robust under 4-bit quantization by adding quantized-forward noise during distillation. Gains: better token-level calibration under Q4.
- Practical thought: we could integrate a tiny distillation step in model onboarding pipeline (post-quantize validation) and store a compact prompt shim in model metadata.

Small experiments I want to run (priority order):
A) Micro KV-cache + optimistic miss path prototype (local GPU LRU 128 tokens)
- Hypothesis: optimistic read path reduces p95 miss penalty by >= 40% vs naive global lock.
- Setup: reuse kvcache-experiments repo (PR#482) on a single A100 node; synthetic chat trace from prod-sample (sanitized).
- Metrics: tokens/sec, median latency, p95 latency on hit vs miss, CPU lock contention.
- Quick commands (sketch):
  - start workload: ./bench/chat_replay --trace traces/prod-sample-2026-09.json --concurrency 40
  - run kvcache server: bazel run //kvcache:server -- --cache-size=128 --optimistic-reads=true
- Owner: Sylas (ask Maya for infra creds)
- Jira: INF-4921 (linked)

B) Tiny microbatcher test against Smart Router baseline
- Hypothesis: p95 stays within 10ms of baseline while cost drops ~7% for conversational QPS 200-1200.
- Variant: static 15ms window vs predictor-based flush.
- Setup: run locally with router simulator, compare to production routing policy.
- Owner: Owen + Sylas. Ticket: INF-4980 (tentative)

Notes on data and risk
- Need to ensure privacy-preserving sampling. Use existing anonymized trace repo (s3://redwood-anon/traces/2026/conv/).
- Watch out for interaction effects: caching changes request interarrival patterns which can affect microbatcher decisions. Tests need to run combined later.

Unresolved questions / ideas to jot down
- Would prefix caching help embedding-only routes? probably not, but an LRU of recent user messages keyed by user-id might help retrieval costs for RAG pipelines.
- Could we expose a per-model "recommended cache depth" heuristic in the model catalog? computed from seed sampling and token reuse stats.
- Eviction policy: LRU vs time-decay vs hybrid (score = recency * reuse_rate). Need a cheap estimator for reuse_rate.

Action items (next 2 weeks)
- [ ] Spin up prototype A (kvcache optimistic reads). Target: reproducible bench and short writeup by 2026-10-14. (Sylas)
- [ ] Simulate microbatcher windows on router traces; collect cost+latency curves. (Owen)
- [ ] Make tiny notebook to scan model catalog for prompt-distill viability; collect 10 candidate open models. (Maya)

Random scraps / heuristics to test later
- Stratify by session length bucket: short (<64 tokens), medium (64-512), long (>512). Cache benefits likely concentrated in medium sessions.
- Measure cold-start cost for private deployments (VPC onprem) — we might need a warmup strategy for dedicated pools.

References / bookmarks
- arXiv:2603.01234 (locality-aware kv caches)
- GitHub PR: redwood-inference/kvcache-experiments#482
- Internal trace: s3://redwood-anon/traces/2026/conv/prod-sample-2026-09.json
- Blog: prompt-space-distillation (May 2026)

Notes-to-self: keep writeups simple; operations will want clear SLO impacts (p50/p95/p99 and cost delta). When in doubt, plot distributions rather than just means.

End of dump.
